text: There is currently no direct PubMed-indexed literature establishing a functional interaction between Griseofulvin and the JAK2 kinase in the context of Polycythemia Vera. Mechanistically, Griseofulvin is primarily known as an antifungal agent that disrupts microtubule dynamics by binding to tubulin, whereas Polycythemia Vera is driven by the constitutive activation of the JAK2/STAT signaling pathway, most commonly via the JAK2 V617F mutation. While some studies suggest that microtubule-targeting agents can indirectly modulate cytokine receptor signaling, any potential inhibitory effect of Griseofulvin on JAK2 would be speculative and lacks empirical validation in clinical or preclinical models of myeloproliferative neoplasms.
